topic: Health Coverage Options for the Medicaid Coverage Gap in Non-Expansion States 2026

title.en: Coverage Gap Under 100% FPL in 2026: Your Options | CoveredUSA
title.es: Brecha de Cobertura Bajo 100% FPL en 2026: Sus Opciones

description.en: Stuck in the coverage gap below 100% FPL in a non-expansion state in 2026? No Medicaid, no subsidies. See every real option, including state programs and CHC.
description.es: Atrapado en la brecha de cobertura bajo el 100% FPL en un estado sin expansion en 2026? Sin Medicaid, sin subsidios. Vea cada opcion real.

h1.en: Stuck in the Coverage Gap in 2026? Here Is What You Can Actually Do.
h1.es: Atrapado en la Brecha de Cobertura en 2026? Esto Es Lo Que Puede Hacer.

subhero.en: If your income is below 100% FPL in a state that did not expand Medicaid, you fall into a gap where ACA subsidies start above you and Medicaid thresholds fall below you. No hard deadline applies, but options exist year-round and some close without warning.
subhero.es: Si su ingreso esta por debajo del 100% FPL en un estado que no expandio Medicaid, cae en una brecha donde los subsidios del ACA comienzan por encima de usted y los umbrales de Medicaid caen por debajo. No hay fecha limite, pero existen opciones durante todo el ano.

heading.en: No federal deadline applies, but some options are year-round and others open only during qualifying events or Open Enrollment.
heading.es: No aplica una fecha limite federal, pero algunas opciones son durante todo el ano y otras se abren solo durante eventos calificadores o la Inscripcion Abierta.

body.en: The Medicaid coverage gap affects roughly 1.5 to 2 million adults in the 10 non-expansion states as of mid-2026. Living in the coverage gap means your income is too high for your state's Medicaid program (which often caps working-adult eligibility well below 50% FPL) but too low to qualify for premium tax credits on the ACA Marketplace (which require income at or above 100% FPL, about $15,960 for one person in 2026). Your options depend on whether you can trigger a qualifying life event SEP, whether your income is near the 100% FPL floor, and whether state-funded or safety-net resources are available where you live.
body.es: La brecha de cobertura de Medicaid afecta a aproximadamente 1.5 a 2 millones de adultos en los 10 estados sin expansion a mediados de 2026. Vivir en la brecha de cobertura significa que su ingreso es demasiado alto para el programa Medicaid de su estado (que a menudo limita la elegibilidad de adultos trabajadores muy por debajo del 50% FPL) pero demasiado bajo para calificar para creditos fiscales de prima en el Mercado ACA (que requieren ingresos al o por encima del 100% FPL, aproximadamente $15,960 para una persona en 2026).

label.es: SEP por evento calificador (perdida de empleo, nacimiento, matrimonio, mudanza a estado con expansion)

quickAnswer.en: If your income is below 100% FPL in one of the 10 states that did not expand Medicaid (Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Kansas, Mississippi, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Wisconsin, or Wyoming), you are in the Medicaid coverage gap. ACA Marketplace subsidies require at least 100% FPL ($15,960 for one person in 2026), and your state's Medicaid program likely caps non-disabled working-adult eligibility far below your income. Four real options exist: (1) move to an expansion state to qualify for Medicaid year-round, which triggers a 60-day Marketplace SEP; (2) get a job with employer-sponsored insurance; (3) use a Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) for sliding-scale care with no insurance required; or (4) try to raise your income to exactly 100% FPL or above so ACA subsidies open up. If you have children, CHIP is available year-round up to 200% to 300% FPL regardless of your state's expansion status.
quickAnswer.es: Si su ingreso esta por debajo del 100% FPL en uno de los 10 estados que no expandieron Medicaid (Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Kansas, Mississippi, Carolina del Sur, Tennessee, Texas, Wisconsin o Wyoming), esta en la brecha de cobertura de Medicaid. Los subsidios del Mercado ACA requieren al menos 100% FPL ($15,960 para una persona en 2026), y el programa Medicaid de su estado probablemente limita la elegibilidad de adultos trabajadores sin discapacidad muy por debajo de su ingreso. Existen cuatro opciones reales: (1) mudarse a un estado con expansion para calificar para Medicaid todo el ano; (2) conseguir un trabajo con seguro del empleador; (3) usar un Centro de Salud Calificado Federalmente (FQHC) para atencion de escala gradual sin seguro; o (4) intentar elevar su ingreso a exactamente el 100% FPL o mas para que se abran los subsidios del ACA.

introParagraphs.en: The Medicaid coverage gap is a structural flaw in the ACA that Congress left unresolved when 10 states chose not to expand Medicaid. Federal law set 100% FPL as the floor for Marketplace premium tax credits because the law assumed every state below that threshold would be covered by expanded Medicaid. When those 10 states refused expansion, adults earning below 100% FPL found themselves in a gap: too high-income for their state's pre-ACA Medicaid program (which in most non-expansion states covers only pregnant women, children, the elderly, and people with severe disabilities at very low income thresholds), and too low-income to qualify for a single dollar of ACA subsidy. In 2026, the gap population in those 10 states sits at roughly 1.5 to 2 million people, per Kaiser Family Foundation (KFF) analysis. The 10 states are Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Kansas, Mississippi, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Wisconsin, and Wyoming. Texas alone accounts for over 700,000 gap adults. Understanding why the gap exists, which resources are still available inside it, and how to exit the gap through income adjustment or geographic relocation is essential for anyone landing on this page.
introParagraphs.es: La brecha de cobertura de Medicaid es una falla estructural en el ACA que el Congreso dejo sin resolver cuando 10 estados decidieron no expandir Medicaid. La ley federal establece el 100% FPL como el piso para los creditos fiscales de prima del Mercado porque la ley suponia que cada estado por debajo de ese umbral estaria cubierto por Medicaid expandido. Cuando esos 10 estados rechazaron la expansion, los adultos que ganaban menos del 100% FPL se encontraron en una brecha: ingresos demasiado altos para el programa Medicaid pre-ACA de su estado (que en la mayoria de los estados sin expansion cubre solo mujeres embarazadas, ninos, ancianos y personas con discapacidades severas con umbrales de ingresos muy bajos), e ingresos demasiado bajos para calificar para un solo dolar de subsidio del ACA. En 2026, la poblacion en la brecha en esos 10 estados es de aproximadamente 1.5 a 2 millones de personas, segun el analisis de la Fundacion Kaiser Family (KFF). Los 10 estados son Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Kansas, Mississippi, Carolina del Sur, Tennessee, Texas, Wisconsin y Wyoming.

introParagraphs.en: Several workarounds exist, though none of them match the clean solution that Medicaid expansion would provide. Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs) operate in every state and provide primary care, dental, behavioral health, and pharmacy services on a sliding-fee scale tied to income. At below 100% FPL, most FQHC visits cost $0 to $40 per encounter, and FQHCs cannot turn away patients based on inability to pay. A second path is the Marketplace itself, but only if your income edges up to or above 100% FPL. At exactly 100% FPL ($15,960 for a single person in 2026), ACA subsidies kick in and can bring a Bronze plan premium to $0 per month after the premium tax credit. A third path is employment: most employer-sponsored insurance plans have employee-share premiums of $100 to $300 per month, with the employer covering 70% to 80% of the full premium under the ACA's employer mandate. Finally, if you have any children in your household, CHIP is year-round and available up to 200% to 300% FPL in all 50 states regardless of the coverage gap. This page maps each option against your exact income, so you know which doors are open and which require taking action first.
introParagraphs.es: Existen varias alternativas, aunque ninguna equivale a la solucion clara que proporcionaria la expansion de Medicaid. Los Centros de Salud Calificados Federalmente (FQHC) operan en todos los estados y brindan atencion primaria, dental, salud conductual y servicios de farmacia en una escala de honorarios variables segun el ingreso. Con menos del 100% FPL, la mayoria de las visitas a los FQHC cuestan de $0 a $40 por encuentro, y los FQHC no pueden rechazar pacientes por incapacidad de pago. Una segunda opcion es el propio Mercado, pero solo si sus ingresos llegan al 100% FPL o lo superan. En exactamente el 100% FPL ($15,960 para una persona sola en 2026), los subsidios del ACA entran en vigor y pueden llevar la prima de un plan Bronze a $0 por mes despues del credito fiscal de prima. Una tercera opcion es el empleo: la mayoria de los planes de seguro patrocinados por el empleador tienen primas de participacion del empleado de $100 a $300 por mes.

name.en: Confirm you are actually in the coverage gap
name.es: Confirme que realmente esta en la brecha de cobertura

text.en: Verify two things: (1) your state is one of the 10 non-expansion states: Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Kansas, Mississippi, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Wisconsin, or Wyoming; and (2) your projected 2026 annual income is below 100% FPL: $15,960 for a single person, $21,640 for a household of 2, $27,320 for 3, or $33,000 for 4. Use the household-size table on this page or the federal poverty level calculator at aspe.hhs.gov. If your income is at or above 100% FPL, ACA Marketplace subsidies are available through healthcare.gov even in a non-expansion state.
text.es: Verifique dos cosas: (1) su estado es uno de los 10 estados sin expansion: Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Kansas, Mississippi, Carolina del Sur, Tennessee, Texas, Wisconsin o Wyoming; y (2) su ingreso anual proyectado para 2026 esta por debajo del 100% FPL: $15,960 para una persona sola, $21,640 para un hogar de 2, $27,320 para 3 o $33,000 para 4. Use la tabla de tamano del hogar en esta pagina o la calculadora del nivel de pobreza federal en aspe.hhs.gov. Si su ingreso esta al o por encima del 100% FPL, los subsidios del Mercado ACA estan disponibles a traves de healthcare.gov incluso en un estado sin expansion.

name.en: Check whether your children qualify for CHIP year-round
name.es: Verifique si sus hijos califican para CHIP durante todo el ano

text.en: CHIP eligibility is entirely separate from the coverage gap. All 10 non-expansion states operate CHIP programs that cover children in households earning up to 200% to 300% FPL. In Texas, CHIP covers children up to 201% FPL. In Florida, up to 210% FPL. In Georgia, up to 247% FPL. In Mississippi, up to 209% FPL. Apply for CHIP any day of the year through healthcare.gov or your state's Children's Medicaid agency. CHIP enrollment has no deadline and no SEP requirement. If you have children under 19 in your household, enroll them in CHIP first before addressing your own coverage gap.
text.es: La elegibilidad para CHIP es completamente separada de la brecha de cobertura. Los 10 estados sin expansion operan programas CHIP que cubren a ninos en hogares que ganan hasta el 200% al 300% FPL. En Texas, CHIP cubre a ninos hasta el 201% FPL. En Florida, hasta el 210% FPL. En Georgia, hasta el 247% FPL. Solicite CHIP cualquier dia del ano a traves de healthcare.gov o la agencia estatal de Medicaid para Ninos de su estado. La inscripcion en CHIP no tiene fecha limite ni requisito de SEP.

name.en: Find a Federally Qualified Health Center for immediate year-round care
name.es: Encuentre un Centro de Salud Calificado Federalmente para atencion inmediata todo el ano

text.en: FQHCs are federally funded health centers that provide primary care, dental, behavioral health, prescriptions, and preventive services regardless of insurance status. Sliding-fee discounts mean most patients below 100% FPL pay $0 to $40 per visit. Use the HRSA Health Center Finder at findahealthcenter.hrsa.gov to locate the nearest FQHC. FQHCs also dispense generics at very low cost under the 340B Drug Pricing Program. This is your primary care solution while you work on the larger insurance problem.
text.es: Los FQHC son centros de salud financiados federalmente que brindan atencion primaria, dental, salud conductual, medicamentos recetados y servicios preventivos independientemente del estado del seguro. Los descuentos de honorarios variables significan que la mayoria de los pacientes por debajo del 100% FPL pagan de $0 a $40 por visita. Use el Localizador de Centros de Salud de HRSA en findahealthcenter.hrsa.gov para ubicar el FQHC mas cercano. Los FQHC tambien dispensan medicamentos genericos a muy bajo costo bajo el Programa de Precios de Medicamentos 340B.

name.en: Calculate whether a small income increase brings you to 100% FPL and opens ACA subsidies
name.es: Calcule si un pequeno aumento de ingresos lo lleva al 100% FPL y abre los subsidios del ACA

text.en: At exactly 100% FPL in 2026, ACA premium tax credits make the benchmark Silver plan cost $0 per month in most non-expansion states. The gap between your current income and 100% FPL may be small. For a single person, 100% FPL is $15,960 annually or about $1,330 per month. Adding part-time work, a side income, or reporting previously overlooked income sources (self-employment, cash wages) can push you to or above the 100% FPL floor. Report your projected income honestly when applying through healthcare.gov. If your income reaches 100% FPL mid-year, a qualifying-event SEP is not required. You can enroll during the next Open Enrollment Period starting November 1, 2026.
text.es: En exactamente el 100% FPL en 2026, los creditos fiscales de prima del ACA hacen que el plan Silver de referencia cueste $0 por mes en la mayoria de los estados sin expansion. La brecha entre su ingreso actual y el 100% FPL puede ser pequena. Para una persona sola, el 100% FPL es $15,960 anuales o aproximadamente $1,330 por mes. Agregar trabajo a tiempo parcial, un ingreso adicional o reportar fuentes de ingresos pasadas por alto puede llevarlo al piso del 100% FPL o por encima. Reporte su ingreso proyectado honestamente al solicitar a traves de healthcare.gov.

name.en: Check whether a qualifying life event opens a 60-day Marketplace SEP
name.es: Verifique si un evento calificador de vida abre un SEP del Mercado de 60 dias

text.en: A qualifying life event (QLE) can trigger a 60-day Special Enrollment Period for the ACA Marketplace even if your income is below 100% FPL, as long as you project your income will reach 100% FPL by year-end or you have access to employer-sponsored insurance. Qualifying events include: losing job-based coverage, having a baby, getting married, being released from incarceration (a qualifying life event per ACA rules), or moving to a new state with different plan availability. Losing Medicaid or CHIP also triggers a 60-day SEP. Apply through healthcare.gov within 60 days of the qualifying event. Coverage typically begins the first day of the following month.
text.es: Un evento calificador de vida (QLE) puede desencadenar un Periodo de Inscripcion Especial de 60 dias para el Mercado ACA incluso si su ingreso esta por debajo del 100% FPL, siempre que proyecte que su ingreso alcanzara el 100% FPL para fin de ano. Los eventos calificadores incluyen: perder cobertura del trabajo, tener un bebe, casarse, ser liberado de encarcelamiento (un evento calificador de vida segun las reglas del ACA), o mudarse a un nuevo estado con diferente disponibilidad de planes. Solicite a traves de healthcare.gov dentro de los 60 dias del evento calificador.

name.en: Consider moving to an expansion state as a long-term solution
name.es: Considere mudarse a un estado con expansion como solucion a largo plazo

text.en: A permanent move to any of the 40 expansion states plus DC triggers a 60-day Marketplace SEP for coverage in your new state. More importantly, in the expansion state, anyone under 138% FPL qualifies for Medicaid year-round. For example, moving from Texas to New Mexico, Louisiana (which expanded in 2016), or Virginia means your sub-100% FPL income immediately qualifies for Medi-Cal-equivalent Medicaid coverage in those states. The move must be permanent (not temporary), and you must establish residency in the new state. Log in to healthcare.gov within 60 days of your move date and select 'I moved to a new state' as your qualifying event.
text.es: Una mudanza permanente a cualquiera de los 40 estados con expansion mas DC desencadena un SEP del Mercado de 60 dias para cobertura en su nuevo estado. Mas importante aun, en el estado con expansion, cualquier persona bajo el 138% FPL califica para Medicaid durante todo el ano. Por ejemplo, mudarse de Texas a Nuevo Mexico, Louisiana o Virginia significa que su ingreso por debajo del 100% FPL califica de inmediato para cobertura de Medicaid en esos estados. La mudanza debe ser permanente, y debe establecer residencia en el nuevo estado. Inicie sesion en healthcare.gov dentro de los 60 dias de su fecha de mudanza.

name.en: If no qualifying event or income increase, plan for Open Enrollment and use safety-net resources in the meantime
name.es: Si no hay evento calificador ni aumento de ingresos, planifique para la Inscripcion Abierta y use recursos de seguridad social mientras tanto

text.en: The next ACA Open Enrollment Period runs November 1, 2026 through January 15, 2027 for 2027 coverage. If your projected 2027 income is at or above 100% FPL, enroll then. Until November, use FQHCs for primary care, apply for prescription assistance through the manufacturer patient assistance programs (PAPs) for any medications you take, and check whether your state has a state-funded coverage program for gap adults. Texas operates Community Health Centers. Florida has KidCare for children (CHIP-equivalent) and limited charity care programs through public hospital networks. Georgia has the Georgia Pathways to Coverage for work-requirement-compliant adults (partial expansion). Alabama has an emergency Medicaid program for qualifying events. Collect documentation of your income situation now so you are ready to enroll quickly at Open Enrollment.
text.es: La proxima Inscripcion Abierta del ACA va del 1 de noviembre de 2026 al 15 de enero de 2027 para cobertura 2027. Si su ingreso proyectado para 2027 es al o por encima del 100% FPL, inscribase entonces. Hasta noviembre, use los FQHC para atencion primaria, solicite asistencia de medicamentos a traves de los programas de asistencia al paciente (PAP) del fabricante para los medicamentos que tome, y verifique si su estado tiene un programa de cobertura financiado por el estado para adultos en la brecha.

The FQHC sliding-fee schedule is federally mandated per Section 330 of the Public Health Service Act. Costs vary by location.
footnote.es: Los subsidios del Mercado ACA requieren ingresos proyectados para 2026 al o por encima del 100% FPL en todos los estados. En los estados sin expansion, no existe una via de subsidio federal para ingresos por debajo del 100% FPL. El calendario de honorarios variables de los FQHC es obligatorio federalmente segun la Seccion 330 de la Ley de Servicio de Salud Publica. Los costos varian segun la ubicacion.

intro.en: The most common and costly mistakes people in the Medicaid coverage gap make in 2026:
intro.es: Los errores mas comunes y costosos que cometen las personas en la brecha de cobertura de Medicaid en 2026:

items.en: Applying for ACA Marketplace subsidies with income below 100% FPL. Healthcare.gov will calculate $0 subsidy and show you a full-price plan you cannot afford. Subsidies require income at or above 100% FPL ($15,960 for one person in 2026). Report your realistic projected income accurately.
items.es: Solicitar subsidios del Mercado ACA con ingresos por debajo del 100% FPL. Healthcare.gov calculara $0 de subsidio y le mostrara un plan de precio completo que no puede pagar. Los subsidios requieren ingresos al o por encima del 100% FPL ($15,960 para una persona en 2026).

items.en: Assuming non-expansion state Medicaid will cover you as an adult without a disability. In all 10 non-expansion states, Medicaid for non-pregnant, non-disabled adults is extremely limited. Texas caps working-adult Medicaid at approximately 18% FPL for parents. Florida does not cover most childless adults regardless of income. Do not assume Medicaid is an option without checking your specific state's limits at medicaid.gov.
items.es: Asumir que Medicaid en el estado sin expansion lo cubrira como adulto sin discapacidad. En los 10 estados sin expansion, Medicaid para adultos no embarazados y sin discapacidad es extremadamente limitado. Texas limita el Medicaid para adultos trabajadores a aproximadamente el 18% FPL para padres. Florida no cubre a la mayoria de los adultos sin hijos independientemente del ingreso.

items.en: Not enrolling children in CHIP. CHIP covers children in households up to 200% to 300% FPL in all 10 non-expansion states, year-round, regardless of whether the adult parent qualifies for any coverage. Missing CHIP enrollment for a child while waiting to resolve adult coverage is a preventable gap.
items.es: No inscribir a los ninos en CHIP. CHIP cubre a ninos en hogares hasta el 200% al 300% FPL en los 10 estados sin expansion, durante todo el ano, independientemente de si el padre adulto califica para alguna cobertura. Perder la inscripcion en CHIP para un nino mientras se espera resolver la cobertura del adulto es una brecha prevenible.

items.en: Not using FQHCs. Federally Qualified Health Centers are available in every county and provide sliding-scale care at $0 to $40 per visit for people below 100% FPL. Many people in the coverage gap are unaware FQHCs exist or assume they need insurance to use them. No insurance is required.
items.es: No usar los FQHC. Los Centros de Salud Calificados Federalmente estan disponibles en cada condado y brindan atencion de escala gradual de $0 a $40 por visita para personas por debajo del 100% FPL. Muchas personas en la brecha de cobertura no saben que existen los FQHC o asumen que necesitan seguro para usarlos.

items.en: Waiting for the federal government to close the gap. Congressional legislation to require all states to expand Medicaid has failed repeatedly. As of mid-2026, no federal mandate for expansion is pending. The coverage gap is a permanent feature of the current law unless individual states choose to expand.
items.es: Esperar a que el gobierno federal cierre la brecha. La legislacion del Congreso para requerir que todos los estados expandan Medicaid ha fallado repetidamente. A mediados de 2026, no hay un mandato federal de expansion pendiente. La brecha de cobertura es una caracteristica permanente de la ley actual a menos que los estados individuales elijan expandirse.

items.en: Missing the 60-day qualifying-event SEP window after a life change. If you lost job-based coverage, had a baby, or got married in the last 60 days, you may have an active SEP right now, even if your income is below 100% FPL, as long as you can project reaching 100% FPL by year-end. Do not let this window close without at least logging in to healthcare.gov to check.
items.es: Perder la ventana de SEP de 60 dias por evento calificador despues de un cambio de vida. Si perdio cobertura del trabajo, tuvo un bebe o se caso en los ultimos 60 dias, puede tener un SEP activo ahora mismo, incluso si su ingreso esta por debajo del 100% FPL, siempre que pueda proyectar alcanzar el 100% FPL para fin de ano.

heading.en: Why the Coverage Gap Exists: The ACA Architecture Flaw in 2026
heading.es: Por Que Existe la Brecha de Cobertura: La Falla de Arquitectura del ACA en 2026

paragraphs.en: Federal law set 100% FPL as the minimum income for ACA Marketplace premium tax credits. Congress made this choice deliberately: the assumption was that Medicaid expansion would cover everyone below 100% FPL. The Supreme Court's 2012 NFIB v. Sebelius ruling made Medicaid expansion optional for states rather than mandatory. When 10 states chose not to expand, the gap snapped open. Pre-ACA Medicaid in non-expansion states typically covers: pregnant women (up to 200% FPL in most states), children under 19 (via CHIP), elderly and disabled adults (via SSI-linked Medicaid), and parents at very low incomes (Texas: 18% FPL, Alabama: 18% FPL, Mississippi: 27% FPL, Florida: 34% FPL). Childless adults without a disability generally qualify for nothing in non-expansion states, regardless of income level, unless a specific categorical program exists.
paragraphs.es: La ley federal establece el 100% FPL como el ingreso minimo para los creditos fiscales de prima del Mercado ACA. El Congreso tomo esta decision deliberadamente: el supuesto era que la expansion de Medicaid cubriria a todos los que estuvieran por debajo del 100% FPL. La decision de la Corte Suprema de 2012 en NFIB v. Sebelius hizo que la expansion de Medicaid fuera opcional para los estados en lugar de obligatoria. Cuando 10 estados decidieron no expandirse, la brecha se abrio. El Medicaid pre-ACA en estados sin expansion tipicamente cubre: mujeres embarazadas (hasta el 200% FPL en la mayoria de los estados), ninos menores de 19 (via CHIP), adultos mayores y con discapacidades (via Medicaid vinculado a SSI), y padres con ingresos muy bajos (Texas: 18% FPL, Alabama: 18% FPL, Mississippi: 27% FPL, Florida: 34% FPL).

paragraphs.en: Three states previously closed their coverage gaps through other means. Louisiana expanded Medicaid in 2016 and no longer has a gap population. North Carolina expanded in December 2023. South Dakota expanded in July 2023. As of June 2026, the remaining 10 non-expansion states are Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Kansas, Mississippi, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Wisconsin, and Wyoming, per the Kaiser Family Foundation Medicaid expansion status tracker. Any state can still opt into expansion at any time by submitting a state plan amendment to CMS, which would make residents immediately eligible for Medicaid at 138% FPL. Georgia adopted a partial expansion in 2023 through its Georgia Pathways to Coverage program, which provides Medicaid to adults aged 19 to 64 who meet a work requirement of 80 hours per month and income up to 100% FPL. As of mid-2026, roughly 11,000 Georgians have enrolled, a fraction of the estimated 300,000 gap adults in that state.
paragraphs.es: Tres estados anteriormente cerraron sus brechas de cobertura por otros medios. Louisiana expandio Medicaid en 2016 y ya no tiene una poblacion en la brecha. Carolina del Norte expandio en diciembre de 2023. Dakota del Sur expandio en julio de 2023. A partir de junio de 2026, los 10 estados sin expansion restantes son Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Kansas, Mississippi, Carolina del Sur, Tennessee, Texas, Wisconsin y Wyoming, segun el rastreador de estado de expansion de Medicaid de la Kaiser Family Foundation.

heading.en: FQHCs and Safety-Net Resources in Non-Expansion States in 2026
heading.es: FQHC y Recursos de Red de Seguridad en Estados sin Expansion en 2026

paragraphs.en: Federally Qualified Health Centers are the primary year-round care solution for coverage-gap adults. HRSA's 2026 data shows more than 1,400 FQHCs operating over 14,000 service sites nationwide, with particularly dense coverage in the 10 non-expansion states given the size of their uninsured populations. Texas has over 130 FQHC organizations. Florida has over 50. Mississippi and Alabama each have dense rural FQHC networks. Services covered under the sliding-fee schedule include: primary care visits, preventive care, immunizations, chronic disease management, behavioral health and substance use disorder treatment, dental care, pharmacy (with 340B pricing), and vision. The sliding-fee discount at below 100% FPL typically results in $0 to $40 per visit depending on the specific FQHC's fee schedule. Locate the nearest FQHC at findahealthcenter.hrsa.gov, which is HRSA's official locator tool, or call 1-877-464-4772.
paragraphs.es: Los Centros de Salud Calificados Federalmente son la principal solucion de atencion medica durante todo el ano para los adultos en la brecha de cobertura. Los datos de HRSA de 2026 muestran mas de 1,400 organizaciones FQHC que operan mas de 14,000 sitios de servicio en todo el pais, con una cobertura particularmente densa en los 10 estados sin expansion dada la magnitud de sus poblaciones sin seguro. Texas tiene mas de 130 organizaciones FQHC. Florida tiene mas de 50. Los servicios cubiertos bajo el programa de honorarios variables incluyen: visitas de atencion primaria, atencion preventiva, inmunizaciones, manejo de enfermedades cronicas, salud conductual y tratamiento de trastornos por uso de sustancias, atencion dental, farmacia (con precios 340B) y vision.

paragraphs.en: Beyond FQHCs, several state-specific safety-net programs exist in the 10 non-expansion states. Texas's Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP) covers children up to 201% FPL. Texas's CHIP Perinatal covers unborn children and extends some prenatal services to mothers. Florida's KidCare program is the CHIP brand covering children up to 210% FPL. Georgia's Pathways to Coverage program provides work-requirement-linked Medicaid to some gap adults. Mississippi operates Ryan White HIV/AIDS Program clinics that provide comprehensive care for people with HIV regardless of insurance status. In all 10 states, public hospital systems and county health departments offer charity care programs for uninsured adults. These programs are not an insurance substitute, but they provide a safety net for acute and episodic care while you work on a longer-term solution.
paragraphs.es: Mas alla de los FQHC, existen varios programas de red de seguridad especificos del estado en los 10 estados sin expansion. El Programa de Seguro de Salud Infantil (CHIP) de Texas cubre a ninos hasta el 201% FPL. CHIP Perinatal de Texas cubre a ninos nonatos y extiende algunos servicios prenatales a las madres. El programa KidCare de Florida es la marca CHIP que cubre a ninos hasta el 210% FPL. El programa Pathways to Coverage de Georgia proporciona Medicaid vinculado a un requisito de trabajo a algunos adultos en la brecha. En los 10 estados, los sistemas hospitalarios publicos y los departamentos de salud del condado ofrecen programas de atencion caritativa para adultos sin seguro.

heading.en: How to Reach the 100% FPL Floor and Unlock ACA Subsidies in 2026
heading.es: Como Alcanzar el Piso del 100% FPL y Desbloquear los Subsidios del ACA en 2026

paragraphs.en: ACA Marketplace subsidies begin at exactly 100% FPL and represent a sharp cliff: at $15,960 annual income for a single person in 2026 ($1,330 per month), premium tax credits drop the benchmark Silver plan to $0 per month in most non-expansion states. At $15,959, there is no subsidy at all. This is why understanding your exact projected income matters. ACA Marketplace subsidies are based on projected Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) for the entire calendar year 2026, not your income at the time of application. If you earn $800 per month from part-time work in January through October and then take a full-time job in November, your projected annual income may be well above 100% FPL for the year even though your monthly income in January looked sub-100%. Project your realistic total 2026 income before applying, and recalculate if circumstances change mid-year.
paragraphs.es: Los subsidios del Mercado ACA comienzan exactamente al 100% FPL y representan un precipicio pronunciado: a $15,960 de ingreso anual para una persona sola en 2026 ($1,330 por mes), los creditos fiscales de prima reducen el plan Silver de referencia a $0 por mes en la mayoria de los estados sin expansion. A $15,959, no hay ningun subsidio. Por eso es importante entender su ingreso proyectado exacto. Los subsidios del Mercado ACA se basan en el Ingreso Bruto Ajustado Modificado (MAGI) proyectado para todo el ano calendario 2026, no su ingreso en el momento de la solicitud.

paragraphs.en: Several income sources count toward MAGI that gap adults commonly overlook. Unemployment compensation counts in full. Self-employment net income counts (revenues minus expenses). Interest and dividends count. Social Security disability income counts for most purposes. Cash wages count even if no W-2 is issued. If you are near the 100% FPL threshold, calculate whether any of these sources bring you above the floor. Report the higher projected income to healthcare.gov: the subsidy you receive will be based on that projection, and you will reconcile it at tax time on Form 8962 using your Form 1095-A. Under-reporting income to stay below 100% FPL does not help you (there is no subsidy below the floor anyway) and creates a tax reconciliation risk if income rises unexpectedly.
paragraphs.es: Varias fuentes de ingresos cuentan para el MAGI que los adultos en la brecha comunmente pasan por alto. La compensacion por desempleo cuenta en su totalidad. Los ingresos netos por trabajo independiente cuentan (ingresos menos gastos). Los intereses y dividendos cuentan. Los ingresos por discapacidad del Seguro Social cuentan para la mayoria de los propositos. Los salarios en efectivo cuentan aunque no se emita un W-2. Si esta cerca del umbral del 100% FPL, calcule si alguna de estas fuentes lo lleva por encima del piso. Reporte el ingreso proyectado mas alto a healthcare.gov.

heading.en: Documents Needed to Apply Once You Have a Coverage Path
heading.es: Documentos Necesarios para Solicitar Una Vez que Tenga una Via de Cobertura

paragraphs.en: Gathering documents in advance significantly speeds up any application. For a Marketplace plan (once income reaches 100% FPL or a qualifying event occurs), you need: photo ID or passport, Social Security numbers for all household members, proof of state residency such as a utility bill or lease dated within 60 days, documentation of projected 2026 income such as recent pay stubs, an employer letter, or a written self-certification for self-employment, and proof of your qualifying event if applying through a SEP (employer termination letter showing last day of coverage, birth certificate, or marriage certificate). For an FQHC, bring photo ID and any income documentation you have. FQHCs accept patients without documentation in many cases and will help with applications. For CHIP enrollment for children, you need: children's Social Security numbers, proof of the child's age (birth certificate), proof of state residency, and documentation of household income.
paragraphs.es: Recopilar documentos con anticipacion acelera significativamente cualquier solicitud. Para un plan del Mercado (una vez que el ingreso alcanza el 100% FPL o se produce un evento calificador), necesita: identificacion con foto o pasaporte, numeros de Seguro Social para todos los miembros del hogar, prueba de residencia en el estado como una factura de servicios o contrato de arrendamiento con fecha dentro de los 60 dias, documentacion del ingreso proyectado para 2026 como recibos de pago recientes, una carta del empleador o una autocertificacion escrita para trabajo independiente, y prueba de su evento calificador si solicita a traves de un SEP. Para CHIP para ninos, necesita: numeros de Seguro Social de los ninos, prueba de la edad del nino (acta de nacimiento), prueba de residencia en el estado y documentacion del ingreso del hogar.

stateRules.rule: Medicaid covers children (CHIP up to 201% FPL), pregnant women (up to 198% FPL), and parents with dependent children (up to 18% FPL). Childless adults without disability are categorically excluded. Texas has not adopted expansion as of June 2026.
Medicaid covers children (KidCare/CHIP up to 210% FPL), pregnant women (up to 191% FPL), and parents (up to 34% FPL). Childless adults are excluded. Florida has not adopted expansion as of June 2026.

Georgia Pathways to Coverage provides Medicaid to adults aged 19 to 64 who meet 80 hours/month work or qualifying-activity requirement and income up to 100% FPL. Approximately 11,000 enrolled as of mid-2026. Georgia Medicaid also covers children via PeachCare for Kids (CHIP) up to 247% FPL.

Medicaid covers children (up to 321% FPL via ALL Kids CHIP), pregnant women (up to 146% FPL), parents (up to 18% FPL), and people with disabilities. Childless adults are categorically excluded without disability. Alabama has not adopted expansion.
Medicaid covers children (CHIP up to 209% FPL), pregnant women (up to 194% FPL), and parents (up to 27% FPL). No childless-adult category. Mississippi has not adopted expansion.
TennCare covers children, pregnant women, and parents under 106% FPL, and people with disabilities. Childless adults are generally ineligible. Tennessee has not adopted ACA Medicaid expansion.

Wisconsin expanded Medicaid for childless adults to 100% FPL under BadgerCare Plus through a pre-ACA waiver, but did not formally adopt ACA expansion to 138% FPL. Adults at 0% to 100% FPL can access BadgerCare Plus. Adults above 100% FPL are directed to the Marketplace. Note: Wisconsin is partially unlike other non-expansion states for this income band.

Medicaid covers children (CHIP up to 209% FPL), pregnant women (up to 194% FPL), parents (up to 67% FPL), and people with disabilities. Childless adults are categorically excluded. South Carolina has not adopted expansion.

KanCare covers children (CHIP up to 238% FPL), pregnant women (up to 166% FPL), parents (up to 38% FPL), and people with disabilities. Childless adults are categorically excluded. Kansas has not adopted expansion.

Medicaid covers children (CHIP up to 200% FPL), pregnant women (up to 159% FPL), parents (up to 54% FPL), and people with disabilities. Childless adults are categorically excluded. Wyoming has not adopted expansion.

en: Applying for ACA Marketplace subsidies with income below 100% FPL: the Marketplace will correctly show $0 subsidy eligibility, not a denial, but the resulting full-price plans are unaffordable for most gap adults. Report 100% FPL or higher only if you genuinely project reaching that income.

Applying for expansion Medicaid in a non-expansion state: the state's system will deny the application because the expansion category does not exist. Verify your state's expansion status at medicaid.gov or kff.org before applying.

Incomplete income documentation causing processing delays: CHIP and non-expansion Medicaid applications require income verification. Submitting without pay stubs or income evidence causes delays of weeks, sometimes months.

Not meeting work requirements for Georgia Pathways: applicants must document 80 hours per month of qualifying activity (work, education, job training, or volunteering). Failing to provide documentation results in denial even if income qualifies.

Immigration status disqualifying from federally-funded Medicaid: most undocumented immigrants are ineligible for full Medicaid (emergency Medicaid only). CHIP rules for lawfully present immigrant children vary by state. Check eligibility rules at healthcare.gov before applying.
es: Solicitar subsidios del Mercado ACA con ingresos por debajo del 100% FPL: el Mercado mostrara correctamente $0 de elegibilidad de subsidio, no una negacion, pero los planes de precio completo resultantes son inasequibles para la mayoria de los adultos en la brecha. Reporte el 100% FPL o mas solo si genuinamente proyecta alcanzar ese ingreso.

Solicitar Medicaid de expansion en un estado sin expansion: el sistema del estado negara la solicitud porque la categoria de expansion no existe. Verifique el estado de expansion de su estado en medicaid.gov o kff.org antes de solicitar.

Documentacion de ingresos incompleta que causa demoras en el procesamiento: las solicitudes de CHIP y Medicaid en estados sin expansion requieren verificacion de ingresos. Presentar sin recibos de pago o evidencia de ingresos causa demoras de semanas, a veces meses.

No cumplir con los requisitos de trabajo para Georgia Pathways: los solicitantes deben documentar 80 horas por mes de actividad calificadora. No proporcionar documentacion resulta en negacion incluso si el ingreso califica.

Estado migratorio que descalifica del Medicaid financiado federalmente: la mayoria de los inmigrantes indocumentados no son elegibles para Medicaid completo (solo Medicaid de emergencia). Las reglas de CHIP para ninos inmigrantes con presencia legal varian segun el estado.

heading.en: Coverage Gap vs Just Above 100% FPL vs Expansion State: What Actually Changes
heading.es: Brecha de Cobertura vs Ligeramente por Encima del 100% FPL vs Estado con Expansion: Que Cambia Realmente

body.en: Three situations look similar on paper but lead to completely different coverage outcomes in 2026. Coverage-gap adults (below 100% FPL in a non-expansion state) have no subsidized insurance path: Medicaid is categorically unavailable for most, and Marketplace subsidies require 100% FPL minimum. The best available options are FQHCs for primary care and CHIP for children. Adults just above 100% FPL in the same non-expansion state face a different situation: ACA subsidies kick in immediately, and at exactly 100% to 150% FPL, a benchmark Silver plan typically costs $0 to $82 per month after the premium tax credit. Adults at the same below-100% FPL income in an expansion state (40 states plus DC) would qualify for Medicaid for free, with comprehensive coverage including prescriptions, dental, and mental health, year-round with no enrollment window. The policy difference is stark: the same household in Houston, Texas versus El Paso, Texas (same state) cannot simply cross the border to trigger expansion eligibility, but a household that relocates from Texas to New Mexico would become immediately eligible for New Mexico's Medicaid expansion for incomes under 138% FPL. The decision matrix for coverage-gap adults is: (1) Can you raise income to 100% FPL? Apply at healthcare.gov during Open Enrollment. (2) Can you move to an expansion state? Do so and enroll in Medicaid. (3) Neither feasible? Use FQHCs for primary care and enroll children in CHIP immediately.
body.es: Tres situaciones parecen similares en papel pero conducen a resultados de cobertura completamente diferentes en 2026. Los adultos en la brecha de cobertura (por debajo del 100% FPL en un estado sin expansion) no tienen una via de seguro subsidiado: Medicaid categoricamente no esta disponible para la mayoria, y los subsidios del Mercado requieren un minimo del 100% FPL. Las mejores opciones disponibles son los FQHC para atencion primaria y CHIP para los ninos. Los adultos ligeramente por encima del 100% FPL en el mismo estado sin expansion enfrentan una situacion diferente: los subsidios del ACA entran en vigor de inmediato, y en exactamente el 100% al 150% FPL, un plan Silver de referencia tipicamente cuesta de $0 a $82 por mes despues del credito fiscal de prima. Los adultos con los mismos ingresos por debajo del 100% FPL en un estado con expansion (40 estados mas DC) calificarian para Medicaid de forma gratuita, con cobertura integral que incluye medicamentos recetados, dental y salud mental, durante todo el ano sin ventana de inscripcion. La matrix de decision para los adultos en la brecha es: (1) Puede aumentar sus ingresos al 100% FPL? Solicite en healthcare.gov durante la Inscripcion Abierta. (2) Puede mudarse a un estado con expansion? Hagalo e inscribase en Medicaid. (3) Ninguno es factible? Use los FQHC para atencion primaria e inscriba a los ninos en CHIP de inmediato.

en.question: What is the Medicaid coverage gap and which states have it in 2026?
en.answer: The Medicaid coverage gap is the income band below 100% FPL where adults in non-expansion states have no access to either Medicaid (income too high for pre-ACA state limits) or ACA Marketplace subsidies (income too low for the 100% FPL floor). As of June 2026, the 10 states with the coverage gap are Alabama, Florida, Georgia (partial exception via Pathways), Kansas, Mississippi, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Wisconsin (partial exception via BadgerCare waiver at 100% FPL), and Wyoming. The gap population is estimated at 1.5 to 2 million adults per KFF analysis. North Carolina (December 2023) and South Dakota (July 2023) closed their gaps by expanding Medicaid.

en.question: Can I get ACA subsidies if my income is below 100% FPL in a non-expansion state?
en.answer: No. ACA Marketplace premium tax credits require income at or above 100% FPL in all states. At $15,959 annual income for a single person in 2026 (one dollar below 100% FPL), the Marketplace subsidy is exactly $0. Healthcare.gov will show you full-price plans ranging from $300 to $800 per month with no subsidy applied. You must project income at or above 100% FPL ($15,960 for one person in 2026) to receive any subsidy. If your projected income is just below the threshold, consider whether additional income sources such as part-time work, self-employment, or cash wages might bring you above the floor.

en.question: What free or low-cost health care can I get without insurance in the coverage gap?
en.answer: Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs) are your primary year-round option for care without insurance. FQHCs provide primary care, dental, behavioral health, and pharmacy services on a sliding-fee scale. At below 100% FPL, most visits cost $0 to $40 per encounter. Use the HRSA Health Center Finder at findahealthcenter.hrsa.gov to locate the nearest FQHC. Community health centers, public hospital charity care programs, and state-funded clinics also provide care. For prescription drugs, manufacturer Patient Assistance Programs (PAPs) provide medications at no cost to qualifying low-income patients. NeedyMeds.org and RxAssist.org maintain PAP directories.

en.question: Do my children qualify for CHIP if I am in the coverage gap?
en.answer: Yes. CHIP eligibility is independent of the adult coverage gap. All 10 non-expansion states operate CHIP programs for children up to 19 years old at income thresholds of 200% to 300% FPL or higher. Texas covers children to 201% FPL, Florida to 210% FPL, Georgia to 247% FPL, Mississippi to 209% FPL, and Alabama to 321% FPL under ALL Kids. CHIP enrollment is year-round with no qualifying event required. Apply through healthcare.gov or your state's CHIP agency. If you have children in your household and they are not already enrolled in CHIP, do that immediately regardless of your own coverage status.

en.question: Does moving to an expansion state get me out of the coverage gap?
en.answer: Yes, permanently. A move to any of the 40 expansion states plus DC removes you from the coverage gap. In those states, Medicaid covers adults with incomes up to 138% FPL ($22,025 for a single person in 2026) year-round with no enrollment window. The move must be a permanent relocation, not a temporary stay. A permanent move to a new state also triggers a 60-day Special Enrollment Period for Marketplace plans, so you have immediate coverage options in the new state. Apply for Medicaid in the new state within days of establishing residency. Coverage typically begins the first of the following month.

en.question: What happens if I have a baby or get married while in the coverage gap?
en.answer: Having a baby or getting married are qualifying life events that open a 60-day Special Enrollment Period for the ACA Marketplace. However, if your income remains below 100% FPL, you still cannot receive subsidies on the Marketplace even with an active SEP. The baby's coverage is handled separately: newborns in households below 100% FPL in non-expansion states may qualify for CHIP depending on the state's CHIP income threshold for infants. Getting married may change your household income calculation, potentially pushing combined household income above 100% FPL and unlocking subsidies. Run the calculation at healthcare.gov before assuming the coverage gap still applies after marriage.

en.question: Is Georgia different from other non-expansion states for the coverage gap?
en.answer: Partially. Georgia's Pathways to Coverage program, launched in July 2023, provides Medicaid to adults aged 19 to 64 who meet a work requirement of 80 hours per month of qualifying activity (employment, job training, education, volunteering, or caregiving) and income up to 100% FPL. As of mid-2026, approximately 11,000 Georgians have enrolled, far below the estimated 300,000 gap adults in the state. The program has significant enrollment barriers including the monthly work-reporting requirement. Eligible Georgians should apply through the Georgia Department of Community Health's Pathways portal at medicaid.georgia.gov. CHIP (PeachCare for Kids) covers Georgia children up to 247% FPL year-round regardless of Pathways eligibility.

en.question: What if my income increases to exactly 100% FPL mid-year? Can I enroll in the Marketplace?
en.answer: An income increase alone does not trigger a qualifying life event SEP for the ACA Marketplace. However, if your projected 2026 annual income reaches 100% FPL or above at any point, you can enroll during the next Open Enrollment Period starting November 1, 2026 for 2027 coverage. If a separate qualifying life event (job change, marriage, birth) occurs around the same time as the income increase, the qualifying event opens the 60-day SEP. When you apply through healthcare.gov, report your projected annual income for the full calendar year, not just your current monthly rate. The subsidy calculation uses your full projected 2026 MAGI.

es.question: Que es la brecha de cobertura de Medicaid y que estados la tienen en 2026?
es.answer: La brecha de cobertura de Medicaid es la banda de ingresos por debajo del 100% FPL donde los adultos en estados sin expansion no tienen acceso ni a Medicaid (ingresos demasiado altos para los limites estatales pre-ACA) ni a los subsidios del Mercado ACA (ingresos demasiado bajos para el piso del 100% FPL). A junio de 2026, los 10 estados con la brecha de cobertura son Alabama, Florida, Georgia (excepcion parcial via Pathways), Kansas, Mississippi, Carolina del Sur, Tennessee, Texas, Wisconsin (excepcion parcial via la exencion de BadgerCare al 100% FPL) y Wyoming. La poblacion en la brecha se estima en 1.5 a 2 millones de adultos segun el analisis de KFF. Carolina del Norte (diciembre 2023) y Dakota del Sur (julio 2023) cerraron sus brechas al expandir Medicaid.

es.question: Puedo obtener subsidios del ACA si mi ingreso esta por debajo del 100% FPL en un estado sin expansion?
es.answer: No. Los creditos fiscales de prima del Mercado ACA requieren ingresos al o por encima del 100% FPL en todos los estados. A $15,959 de ingreso anual para una persona sola en 2026 (un dolar por debajo del 100% FPL), el subsidio del Mercado es exactamente $0. Healthcare.gov le mostrara planes de precio completo que van de $300 a $800 por mes sin subsidio aplicado. Debe proyectar ingresos al o por encima del 100% FPL ($15,960 para una persona en 2026) para recibir cualquier subsidio. Si su ingreso proyectado esta justo por debajo del umbral, considere si fuentes adicionales de ingresos podrian llevarlo por encima del piso.

es.question: Que atencion medica gratuita o de bajo costo puedo obtener sin seguro en la brecha de cobertura?
es.answer: Los Centros de Salud Calificados Federalmente (FQHC) son su principal opcion durante todo el ano para atencion sin seguro. Los FQHC brindan atencion primaria, dental, salud conductual y servicios de farmacia en una escala de honorarios variables. Con menos del 100% FPL, la mayoria de las visitas cuestan de $0 a $40 por encuentro. Use el Localizador de Centros de Salud de HRSA en findahealthcenter.hrsa.gov para encontrar el FQHC mas cercano. Para medicamentos, los Programas de Asistencia al Paciente (PAP) del fabricante proporcionan medicamentos sin costo a pacientes de bajos ingresos calificados.

es.question: Califican mis hijos para CHIP si estoy en la brecha de cobertura?
es.answer: Si. La elegibilidad para CHIP es independiente de la brecha de cobertura de adultos. Los 10 estados sin expansion operan programas CHIP para ninos hasta 19 anos en umbrales de ingresos del 200% al 300% FPL o mas altos. Texas cubre ninos hasta el 201% FPL, Florida hasta el 210% FPL, Georgia hasta el 247% FPL, Mississippi hasta el 209% FPL y Alabama hasta el 321% FPL bajo ALL Kids. La inscripcion en CHIP es durante todo el ano sin necesidad de un evento calificador. Solicite a traves de healthcare.gov o la agencia CHIP de su estado.

es.question: Mudarse a un estado con expansion me saca de la brecha de cobertura?
es.answer: Si, permanentemente. Una mudanza a cualquiera de los 40 estados con expansion mas DC lo saca de la brecha de cobertura. En esos estados, Medicaid cubre a adultos con ingresos hasta el 138% FPL ($22,025 para una persona sola en 2026) durante todo el ano sin ventana de inscripcion. La mudanza debe ser una reubicacion permanente. Una mudanza permanente a un nuevo estado tambien desencadena un Periodo de Inscripcion Especial de 60 dias para planes del Mercado, por lo que tiene opciones de cobertura inmediatas en el nuevo estado.

es.question: Que pasa si tengo un bebe o me caso mientras estoy en la brecha de cobertura?
es.answer: Tener un bebe o casarse son eventos calificadores de vida que abren un Periodo de Inscripcion Especial de 60 dias para el Mercado ACA. Sin embargo, si su ingreso sigue siendo inferior al 100% FPL, todavia no puede recibir subsidios en el Mercado incluso con un SEP activo. La cobertura del bebe se maneja por separado: los recien nacidos en hogares por debajo del 100% FPL en estados sin expansion pueden calificar para CHIP segun el umbral de ingresos CHIP del estado. Casarse puede cambiar el calculo de ingresos del hogar, potencialmente empujando el ingreso combinado del hogar por encima del 100% FPL y desbloqueando subsidios.

es.question: Es Georgia diferente de otros estados sin expansion para la brecha de cobertura?
es.answer: Parcialmente. El programa Pathways to Coverage de Georgia, lanzado en julio de 2023, proporciona Medicaid a adultos de 19 a 64 anos que cumplen un requisito de trabajo de 80 horas por mes de actividad calificadora (empleo, capacitacion laboral, educacion, voluntariado o cuidado) e ingresos hasta el 100% FPL. A mediados de 2026, aproximadamente 11,000 georgianos se han inscrito, muy por debajo de los estimados 300,000 adultos en la brecha en ese estado. Los georgianos elegibles deben solicitar a traves del portal Pathways del Departamento de Salud Comunitaria de Georgia en medicaid.georgia.gov.

es.question: Que pasa si mis ingresos aumentan a exactamente el 100% FPL a mitad de ano? Puedo inscribirme en el Mercado?
es.answer: Un aumento de ingresos por si solo no desencadena un SEP de evento calificador para el Mercado ACA. Sin embargo, si su ingreso anual proyectado para 2026 alcanza el 100% FPL o mas en cualquier momento, puede inscribirse durante la proxima Inscripcion Abierta que comienza el 1 de noviembre de 2026 para cobertura 2027. Si ocurre un evento calificador de vida separado al mismo tiempo que el aumento de ingresos, el evento calificador abre el SEP de 60 dias. Al solicitar a traves de healthcare.gov, reporte su ingreso anual proyectado para el ano calendario completo, no solo su tasa mensual actual.
